outOfScope: evaluating a real company or person

claims.claim: OpenStax describes shareholders as owners of stock and stakeholders as individuals or groups affected by business decisions; it presents shareholder-focused and stakeholder-focused approaches as competing views.
OpenStax explains that law does not capture every ethical responsibility and presents corporate social responsibility as a way businesses may consider broader social and environmental effects.

The G20/OECD Principles identify board responsibilities, disclosure and transparency, shareholder rights, stakeholders, sustainability, and resilience as corporate-governance topics for policy frameworks.

OpenStax uses conflict of interest for personal, financial, or other interests that can influence a person's ability to perform organizational duties and describes disclosure or avoidance as common code-of-conduct approaches.

A legal minimum and an ethical judgment are different categories: legal compliance asks what the law requires, while ethics can ask how interests, impacts, and reasons should be assessed when the law is not dispositive.
This lesson presents governance tools and ethical frameworks descriptively; their use and legal effect vary by jurisdiction, organization, facts, and applicable rules.

conflictingEvidence: The source material describes more than one lens for corporate purpose. This lesson does not resolve the shareholder-focused and stakeholder-focused views into a single required corporate objective.
unsupportedExistingClaims: No existing draft was treated as factual authority.
correctionsNeeded: Kept governance, legal compliance, and ethical evaluation distinct.
Presented CSR and stakeholder analysis as frameworks rather than a measure of any real company's character.
Excluded advice about responding to an actual conflict or meeting a legal compliance duty.
rightsIssues: All sources are used as reference-only sources. The lesson is original synthesis and does not adapt source prose, model policies, or legal text.
